r1: overruled correctness at .artifacts/worktrees/t1/.claude/workflows/build-implement.js:277: AC-16 requires that needs_from_sibling routing to boundaryRepair happen BEFORE the emptyDiffAction loop runs (execution order), not that the function declarations appear in that textual order. Both emptyDiffAction and boundaryRepair are ordinary `function` declarations, which are hoisted in JavaScript, so their position in the source text has no effect on execution order. The fixer's dispute correctly shows the actual call sites (boundaryRepair consulted via routing at line 830, emptyDiffAction called at line 841) satisfy the spec's real, execution-order requirement. No test in substrate/test (checked boundary-wiring.test.js and others) asserts a source-declaration-order constraint between these two names, and the finding's own evidence is a textual indexOf comparison of function declarations, not a check of invocation order. This finding checks an irrelevant property and does not name a real defect in the implementation.

r1: overruled correctness at .artifacts/tests/t1/b5-suite-hygiene.test.js:1: AC-22's full-suite pass is scoped as a post-landing check, and substrate/test/ landing happens only at the Integrate barrier via the existing mechanical landing step once a workflow run with passing tasks reaches that point — no Integrate run has executed for t1, so substrate/test/ correctly lacking b5-*.test.js files at this stage in the fix loop is expected pre-integration state, not a defect in the implementation. Additionally, the spec's exclusions explicitly place substrate/test/ contents ("The tests under substrate/test/ ... are the Test Author's surface, not the implementer's, and are deliberately left out of touched_surfaces") outside the implementer's owned surfaces, so demanding the implementer land files there would itself exceed scope. The finding faults expected, spec-required sequencing/scope rather than a real defect in build-implement.js, build-spec.js, contracts.schema.json, or implementer.md.

escalations.hypothesis: The loop is stuck because neither leftover finding can be closed by the fixer inside the spec. Both went past the fixer cap in r1 and were never fixed, disputed or overruled. AC-17-19's "checkCriterionCoupling is not defined" failure sits in substrate/test/graph-lint-helpers.js. The spec excludes that file as the Test Author's surface, so the bug is in the test loader, not in build-spec.js. The repeated AC-13 finding (medium, correctness, still open) comes from ambiguous spec wording. AC-13 lists "wait" as a kind of repair attempt, but its outcome enum has no value for a wait on its own. That leaves open whether a wait that leads to a rerun should add its own boundary_repairs entry. It also matches the fact that the only pushes happen on rerun and escalate. Both lenses in the r2c confirmation round were silent on these two findings, and silence is not evidence that they are resolved.
